title: Identifiable Lindblad-style latent neural dynamics
objective: Test whether low-dimensional open-system dynamics provide more identifiable and intervention-predictive latent trajectories than classical dynamical controls.
decision_gates: Synthetic promotion requires median normalized recovery error <=0.20 for identifiable Hamiltonian/collapse parameters at the preregistered moderate-SNR tier and no systematic sign inversion.
Real-data comparisons must include LDS/Kalman, VAR/damped-oscillator, switching-state, and a flexible nonlinear control when sample size permits.
A mechanistic claim requires held-out predictive improvement plus bootstrap parameter stability (target ICC >=0.60) and intervention-direction consistency.
If a classical state-space model matches predictive performance and produces more stable parameters, the Lindblad parameterization is not promoted.
No fitted latent collapse/dephasing parameter may be interpreted as microscopic biological decoherence without an independent physical measurement.
